content.text:
Finding submitted.

**Summary:** Section 6.3 does contain a vendor-side (Servicer/Marketing Agent) indemnity running to the Issuer and the trustees, with a workable notice/defence procedure in 6.3(b)–(c) and a recoupment mechanic in 6.3(d). But it is triggered only by willful misconduct, bad faith or gross negligence — there is no third-party intellectual-property infringement cover anywhere in the document (no "infringe", "intellectual property" or "hold harmless" language exists), and no procure/modify/replace/refund remedy set. Under the detection guidance, a vendor indemnity that excludes IP infringement fails the fallback, so I classified this as a **deviation**.

The redline is a single inserted Section 6.3(e) at the fallback level, carrying only the seven fallback elements: the IP indemnity to the existing "Indemnified Persons", the modification/combination/specification exclusions, procure-modify-replace, refund of Servicing Fees, and a three-times-annual-Servicing-Fee cap drafted to bite only on the new subsection so our existing uncapped 6.3(a) indemnity is not weakened. I did not touch the Depositor's own defend-title covenant in Section 9.2 (which benefits the counterparty's chain but is our covenant, not a flaggable term), and did not upgrade to the preferred duty-to-defend/data-breach package, which would have required extensive collateral drafting in a securitisation structure.
